A BepInEx that is already here is brought into its care the same way, with a copy of everything replaced kept beside the install; your mods, mod configs and BepInEx.cfg are left as they are, and so is your doorstop_config.ini unless the new pack needs a different one. An install another mod manager drives is never touched. Every server on this install shares one BepInEx, so this covers all of them.

hearth.upkeep.hexium.note.lore: Hexium is a second mod site. Whoever runs it is not named on the site, and its accounts are Discord sign-ins, so BakaLoader cannot tell you that an author there is the same person as the author of the same name on Thunderstore. With this on, your machine contacts hexium.gg about four times an hour while BakaLoader is open, and that site says it keeps request logs for up to ninety days. herald.head.sub.lore: one Discord post · edits itself · never floods the channel

herald.wiz.title.lore: Guided setup: create a webhook in Discord, paste it here, choose what to share, publish the first post

herald.intro.body.lore: BakaLoader keeps {one} status post in your Discord channel and quietly edits it whenever the realm changes: players joining, mods updating, the next restart drawing near. One post, forever fresh. No spam.
herald.intro.body.plain: BakaLoader keeps {one} status post in your Discord channel and quietly edits it whenever the world changes: players joining, mods updating, the next restart drawing near. One post, forever fresh. No spam.

herald.sharing.toggle.title.lore: Master switch. On: the status post keeps itself up to date. Off: nothing is ever sent.

herald.field.webhook.title.lore: In Discord: Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → pick a channel → Copy Webhook URL. The setup wizard walks you through it.

herald.field.thread.title.lore: Optional. Only for posting inside a thread or forum post: right-click the thread → Copy Thread ID (needs Discord developer mode, under App Settings → Advanced). Blank = post directly in the channel.

herald.thread.placeholder.lore: optional · blank = post in the channel itself

herald.carries.note.lore: Always: server name, status, players online, world, mod count, last mod update, next restart. Optional extras:

herald.share.address.title.lore: Include the server's public IP and port so friends copy it straight from Discord.

herald.share.password.title.lore: Include the password in the post. Anyone who can read the channel sees it, so use it only for private channels.

herald.share.password.warn.lore: ᚦ the password is visible to everyone in that channel, so trusted halls only

herald.share.events.title.lore: Also send one-off messages when the server starts, stops or crashes, and when vikings join or leave. These are separate messages, not edits of the status post.
herald.share.events.title.plain: Also send one-off messages when the server starts, stops or crashes, and when players join or leave. These are separate messages, not edits of the status post.

herald.share.events.note.lore: one-off messages for start · stop · crash · join · leave

herald.publish.title.lore: Create the status post now, or refresh it immediately if it already exists

herald.remove.title.lore: Delete the status post from Discord. Settings stay, so you can publish again any time.

skald.reset.title.lore: Clear every counted number and start the journal again

cond.backup.body.lore: The worlds could not be copied aside, so the server was not started.

cond.crash.body.relaunch.lore: The server process stopped on its own. BakaLoader is relaunching it.

cond.crash.body.down.lore: The server process stopped on its own. It stays down until you start it.

cond.plugin.body.lore: A plugin BakaLoader installs alongside the server could not be put in place.

cond.restart.body.lore: Saved settings differ from what the running server started with. They apply at the next restart.

cond.appupd.manual.idle.lore: It will not install on its own. Install it now with Update BakaLoader, or turn auto-update on in Upkeep and it goes in the next time you close the app.

cond.appupd.auto.lore: It installs the next time you close the app.

cond.appupd.checking_off.lore: Update checking is off in Upkeep, so nothing installs itself until you turn it back on.

cond.launch.update_failed.lore: The update did not finish: {reason}. The server was not started.

cond.launch.dismissed.toast.lore: Left as it is · the server stays down until you start it

cond.save.msg.lore: The server could not write the world to disk. {body}

cond.save.msg.timed.lore: The server could not write the world to disk ({ms}ms). {body}

bepinex.reason.servers_running.lore: BakaLoader counts these servers as loading this same BepInEx, so nothing is written while one of them is up. Still up: {names}.

bepinex.reason.not_a_loader.lore: That download is not a BepInEx pack, so nothing was written.

bepinex.reason.integrity.lore: The BepInEx download did not match what the site listed, so nothing was written.

bepinex.reason.too_large.lore: That download is larger than BakaLoader will fetch for a loader, so it was stopped.

bepinex.reason.offline.lore: Thunderstore did not answer, so BepInEx could not be fetched.

bepinex.reason.busy.lore: BepInEx is already being written. Try again in a moment.

bepinex.reason.no_server_path.lore: Set a valid server .exe path before installing BepInEx.

bepinex.reason.no_wrong_folder.lore: There is no misplaced BepInEx folder to remove.

bepinex.reason.locked.lore: Something has {file} open, so nothing was written. Stop every server on this install, close anything reading that folder, and try again.

bepinex.reason.newer.lore: The BepInEx here ({installed}) is newer than the pack Thunderstore offers ({pack}), so nothing was written.

bepinex.reason.core_is_junction.lore: This server's BepInEx core is a link to the install it shares, so the write belongs on that install instead.

bepinex.reason.unrecognised_core.lore: There is a BepInEx beside this server that BakaLoader does not recognise, so nothing was written over it.

bepinex.reason.no_backup.lore: There is no saved copy of BepInEx here to put back.

bepinex.reason.write_failed.lore: BepInEx could not be written here. The log has the reason your machine gave, and a copy of anything that was replaced is in the backups folder beside the install.

bepinex.reason.outside_unconfirmed.lore: BakaLoader did not put the BepInEx that is beside this server, so nothing was written over it without asking you first.

bepinex.reason.driven_elsewhere.lore: Another mod manager drives the BepInEx beside this server, so nothing was written over it. Writing here would swap the whole mod set that tool looks after.

bepinex.reason.foreign_core.lore: The BepInEx here ({installed}) is not the framework this pack carries, so nothing was written over it.

bepinex.reason.prerelease.lore: The newest BepInEx pack ({version}) is a pre-release, so a restart will not put it in on its own. You can still install it by hand.

bepinex.reason.deprecated.lore: Thunderstore has flagged this BepInEx package as one to move away from, so nothing was written and the install was left as it was.

bepinex.reason.pulled.lore: Thunderstore has taken BepInEx {version} down, so a restart will not put it in. The install was left exactly as it was.

bepinex.reason.soak.lore: BepInEx {version} came out too recently for a restart to put it in unwatched. A restart after {when} will take it, and you can install it by hand before then.

bepinex.reason.unverified.lore: Thunderstore did not say how large the BepInEx {version} download should be, so there was nothing to check it against and nothing was written.

bepinex.reason.drift.lore: Something other than BakaLoader has written to the BepInEx beside this server since BakaLoader put it there, so it stopped looking after it and nothing was written.

bepinex.reason.repair_mismatch.lore: The BepInEx {version} that came down does not match, file for file, what BakaLoader recorded when it installed that version, so nothing was put back.

bepinex.reason.repair_pack_gone.lore: This install was written from BepInEx {noted}, and Thunderstore does not serve that pack any more, so the files that went could not be put back. The pack it serves now is {offered}, and Update takes that one instead.

bepinex.notice.already_maintained.lore: BakaLoader keeps BepInEx up to date for every server on this install, so there is nothing to put in by hand.

bepinex.notice.written.title.lore: BepInEx was updated at a restart

bepinex.notice.written.body.lore: BepInEx went from {from} to {to}. A copy of every file that was replaced is in {folder}.

bepinex.notice.written.body.first.lore: BepInEx {to} was put in at a restart. Anything it replaced is kept in the BepInEx backups folder beside the install.

bepinex.notice.healed.title.lore: A BepInEx write here did not finish

bepinex.notice.healed.body.lore: A write to BepInEx stopped part way, so BakaLoader put the copy from before it back. The loader here is the one you had, and nothing was updated.

bepinex.condition.waiting.body.lore: BepInEx {version} is ready and goes in once every server on this install has stopped, because they all load the same one. Still up: {names}.

bepinex.condition.waiting.body.none.lore: BepInEx {version} is ready and goes in at the next restart window, once every server on this install has stopped, because they all load the same one.

bepinex.condition.left_alone.title.lore: BepInEx was left as it was

bepinex.condition.no_mods.title.lore: This world is running without its mods

lore.one: BepInEx is not loading here, so the {count} mod on this server is doing nothing and the people on it are playing plain Valheim. Stop the server, put BepInEx back, and start it again.
lore.other: BepInEx is not loading here, so all {count} mods on this server are doing nothing and the people on it are playing plain Valheim. Stop the server, put BepInEx back, and start it again.

bepinex.condition.not_loaded.body.lore: This server has been up a while and BepInEx never wrote its log, so no mod is loaded. The wiki page says what to check.

bepinex.row.state.missing.lore: Not installed, so nothing in this list would load.

bepinex.row.state.maintained.lore: Kept up to date by BakaLoader.

bepinex.row.state.manual.lore: BakaLoader put this pack in and is not looking after it.

bepinex.row.state.outside.lore: Installed outside BakaLoader, so there is no telling whether a newer pack is out.

bepinex.row.state.drifted.lore: BakaLoader installed this BepInEx and something else has changed it since, so BakaLoader has stopped looking after it and writes nothing here until you press Update.

bepinex.row.state.elsewhere.lore: Another mod manager drives this BepInEx, so BakaLoader leaves it alone.

bepinex.row.state.foreign.lore: The BepInEx here ({version}) is not the framework the pack BakaLoader installs carries, so it is left alone.

bepinex.row.state.unrecognised.lore: There is a BepInEx folder here that BakaLoader does not recognise, and nothing in it loads mods.

bepinex.row.state.damaged.lore: The BepInEx folder here is missing the file that loads everything else, so no mod would load.

bepinex.row.state.incomplete.lore: {file} is gone from this install, so BepInEx would not load. An antivirus taking that file is the usual cause.

bepinex.row.version.pack.title.lore: The Thunderstore pack version, read from the note BakaLoader writes beside the install.

bepinex.row.version.file.title.lore: The loader's own file version. Nothing on disk records which pack it came in, so a pack bump cannot be seen from here.

bepinex.row.note.next_check.lore: Checked again at every scheduled restart.

bepinex.row.note.waiting.lore: Version {version} is ready and goes in once every server on this install has stopped.

lore.one: Counted as loading this same BepInEx as {count} other server.
lore.other: Counted as loading this same BepInEx as {count} other servers.

bepinex.row.note.busy.lore: BepInEx is being written right now.

bepinex.row.note.wrong_folder.lore: A BepInEx pack was unpacked under the plugins folder, where it does nothing at all.

bepinex.row.note.brought_in.lore: You have said yes to BakaLoader looking after BepInEx, so this install is brought into its care at the next scheduled restart.

bepinex.row.note.interrupted_write.lore: A write here did not finish and the mark it left is still on disk. BakaLoader tries to settle it every time it reads this install, so something is still holding the note beside these files, and that is why an install it wrote can read as one it did not. Stop every server on this install, close anything reading that folder, then press the button on this row.

bepinex.row.blocked.title.lore: Stop the servers that are up first. BakaLoader counts them as loading this same BepInEx.

bepinex.row.updated.toast.lore: BepInEx went from {from} to {to}. The files it replaced are in {folder}.

bepinex.row.already_current.toast.lore: BepInEx {version} is already the pack Thunderstore offers, so nothing was written.

bepinex.row.adopted.toast.lore: The BepInEx here already matched pack {version} file for file, so BakaLoader took it into its care without writing over anything.

bepinex.row.restored.toast.lore: BepInEx was put back from the copy saved on {stamp}.

bepinex.row.doorstop_replaced.toast.lore: The new pack needed its own doorstop_config.ini, so yours went into the backup with everything else that was replaced.

bepinex.row.removed.toast.lore: The misplaced BepInEx folder was removed.

bepinex.add.pack_installed.toast.lore: That link is the loader itself, so BepInEx was installed rather than added as a mod.

bepinex.dialog.first.title.existing.lore: BepInEx is already here. Let BakaLoader look after it?

bepinex.dialog.first.body.lore: BepInEx is the loader every mod runs under. BakaLoader can put it in when it is missing and move it to a newer pack during a scheduled restart.

bepinex.dialog.first.body.outside.lore: This install already has BepInEx (core {version}), put in by you or by another tool. Say yes and BakaLoader brings it into its care at the next scheduled restart: it replaces the BepInEx core and the loader files beside the server with the current pack from Thunderstore, and moves it to a newer pack whenever one comes out.

bepinex.dialog.first.body.outside.novers.lore: There is already a BepInEx beside this server, put in by you or by another tool. Say yes and BakaLoader brings it into its care at the next scheduled restart: it replaces the BepInEx core and the loader files beside the server with the current pack from Thunderstore, and moves it to a newer pack whenever one comes out.

bepinex.dialog.first.body.elsewhere.lore: Another mod manager drives the BepInEx beside this server: its own doorstop_config.ini points at that tool's profile folder. BakaLoader leaves this install alone whichever way you answer, because writing here would swap the whole mod set that tool looks after. Your answer covers any BepInEx you ask BakaLoader for later.

bepinex.dialog.first.body.foreign.lore: The BepInEx beside this server (core {version}) is not the framework the pack BakaLoader installs carries. BakaLoader leaves this install alone whichever way you answer. Your answer covers any BepInEx you ask BakaLoader for later.

bepinex.dialog.first.kept.lore: Your BepInEx.cfg, every mod, every mod config and the patchers folder are left exactly as they are. Your doorstop_config.ini is kept too, unless the new pack needs a different one, and then yours goes into the backup with everything else. A copy of everything BakaLoader replaces goes into BepInEx\.bakaloader-bepinex-backups first.

bepinex.dialog.first.no_write.lore: Say no and BakaLoader never writes to it.

bepinex.dialog.first.note.lore: One BepInEx is shared by every server on this install, so this answer covers all of them. It can be changed any time in Upkeep.

bepinex.dialog.first.yes.toast.lore: BakaLoader will look after BepInEx from here on.

bepinex.dialog.first.no.toast.lore: BepInEx is yours to put in and keep current.

bepinex.dialog.install.body.lore: Nothing loads a mod until BepInEx is in place. BakaLoader fetches the pack below and writes it beside the server executable, then finishes the add you started.

bepinex.dialog.install.note.lore: Leave the address as it is unless you have a reason not to. Another link has to be a BepInEx pack of the same shape, or nothing is written.

bepinex.dialog.install.running.warn.lore: Every server on this install loads the same BepInEx, so the write is refused while one is up. Still up: {names}.

bepinex.dialog.remove.body.lore: This folder is a BepInEx pack unpacked where mods go. It loads nothing there, and removing it leaves the real install alone.

bepinex.dialog.takeover.title.lore: Write BepInEx over the install that is here?

bepinex.dialog.takeover.body.lore: The BepInEx beside this server is core {installed}, and BakaLoader did not put it there. Saying yes replaces the core and the loader files with Thunderstore pack {pack}.

bepinex.dialog.takeover.body.unknown_pac.lore: The BepInEx beside this server is core {installed}, and BakaLoader did not put it there. Saying yes replaces the core and the loader files with the pack Thunderstore offers when the write runs.

bepinex.dialog.takeover.elsewhere.lore: Another mod manager drives this install. Writing here swaps the whole mod set that tool looks after, and it will not know.

bepinex.dialog.takeover.foreign.lore: What is here is not the framework this pack carries, so writing over it changes which BepInEx your mods run under.

bepinex.dialog.takeover.unrecognised.lore: There is a BepInEx folder here that BakaLoader does not recognise. Whatever is in it is replaced, and a copy goes into the backups folder first.

bepinex.dialog.takeover.drifted.lore: Something else has written to this BepInEx since BakaLoader put it there, so whatever it changed is replaced.

bepinex.dialog.downgrade.body.lore: The BepInEx here ({installed}) is newer than the pack Thunderstore offers ({pack}). Saying yes moves this install backwards, and a mod built for the newer one may stop loading.

bepinex.dialog.restore.title.lore: Put the saved copy of BepInEx back?

bepinex.dialog.restore.body.lore: This puts back the copy BakaLoader saved on {stamp}, which is the loader exactly as it was before the last write. Your mods, mod configs and BepInEx.cfg are not touched.

bepinex.dialog.restore.own.lore: There is also the BepInEx you had before BakaLoader, saved on {stamp} when this install came into its care. That copy is kept for good while the others roll over.

bepinex.dialog.restore.own.version.lore: There is also the BepInEx you had before BakaLoader, core {version}, saved on {stamp} when this install came into its care. That copy is kept for good while the others roll over.

bepinex.dialog.restore.own.ok.lore: Put my own BepInEx back instead

bepinex.progress.phase.checking.lore: Checking what came down against what the site listed.

bepinex.progress.phase.linking.lore: Sharing it with every server on this install.

realm.adopt.mods.label.plain: Copy the active world's mods into it

realm.new.iso.title.lore:
ON: this realm gets its own BepInEx: its own mods, mod configs, and cache, fully independent of your other servers. Example: run Epic Loot here while your main server stays vanilla, or trial a mod update without risking the live world. The bulky game files are shared behind the scenes, so this does NOT duplicate the multi-gigabyte install.

OFF: the realm runs from the same install and mod folder as the base server: installing, updating, or removing a mod on either one changes both.
realm.new.iso.title.plain:
ON: this world gets its own BepInEx: its own mods, mod configs, and cache, fully independent of your other servers. Example: run Epic Loot here while your main server stays vanilla, or trial a mod update without risking the live world. The bulky game files are shared behind the scenes, so this does NOT duplicate the multi-gigabyte install.

OFF: the world runs from the same install and mod folder as the base server: installing, updating, or removing a mod on either one changes both.

realm.new.seedmods.title.lore:
ON: the new realm starts with a copy of the current server's mods and their configs, then goes its own way: updating or removing a mod here never touches the original. Example: clone your main server's whole mod set to build a matching test server.

OFF: the realm starts clean with no mods; add them later in the MODS hall.

Only applies with a separate install. On a shared install the mods are shared by definition.

Only applies with a separate install. On a shared install the mods are shared by definition.

realm.new.savedir.title.lore:
ON: this realm keeps its worlds and backups in its own save folder, so two servers can never write to the same world file and backups never mix. Example: Midgard Two saves under its own folder instead of the shared IronGate\Valheim one.

OFF: the realm uses the shared Valheim save folder. That works, as long as two realms never host the same world at the same time (BakaLoader warns if they would).

herald.wiz.intro.body.lore: The Herald keeps one status post in a Discord channel of your choosing and quietly edits that same post whenever the realm changes. It never sends a stream of messages, so your channel stays clean.
herald.wiz.intro.body.plain: Discord sharing keeps one status post in a Discord channel of your choosing and quietly edits that same post whenever the world changes. It never sends a stream of messages, so your channel stays clean.

herald.wiz.intro.choose.body.lore: whether the join address, the password, and one-off event posts are included.

herald.wiz.intro.need.body.lore: a Discord server where you can manage webhooks (or a friendly admin who can). Takes about a minute.

herald.wiz.hook.body.lore: A webhook is a private posting address for one channel. In Discord:

herald.wiz.hook.step1.lore: open your Discord server and click its name → Server Settings

herald.wiz.hook.step3.lore: name it (say, BakaLoader Herald) and pick the channel the post should live in
herald.wiz.hook.step3.plain: name it (say, BakaLoader) and pick the channel the post should live in

herald.wiz.hook.step4.lore: press Copy Webhook URL and paste it below

herald.wiz.hook.stat.idle.lore: paste the URL · the Herald will knock on it to make sure it answers
herald.wiz.hook.stat.idle.plain: paste the URL · BakaLoader will test it to make sure it answers

herald.wiz.hook.stat.bad.lore: that webhook does not answer · re-copy the URL from Discord

herald.wiz.hook.thread.note.lore: Thread ID is only for posting inside a thread or forum post: right-click the thread → Copy Thread ID (needs Developer Mode, under App Settings → Advanced). Most people leave this blank.

herald.wiz.share.body.lore: The post always shows name, status, players, world, mods and the next restart. Decide what else rides along. Everything can be changed later in the HERALD hall.
herald.wiz.share.body.plain: The post always shows name, status, players, world, mods and the next restart. Decide what else rides along. Everything can be changed later in the DISCORD hall.

herald.wiz.share.password.title.lore: Include the password in the post. Anyone who can read the channel sees it.

herald.wiz.share.password.warn.lore: everyone in that channel will see the password, so use private channels only

herald.wiz.share.events.title.lore: Also send one-off messages for server start/stop/crash and player join/leave. Separate messages, not edits of the status post.

herald.wiz.share.events.note.lore: Event posts are extra one-off messages (start · stop · crash · join · leave). Leave off for the single silent status post only.

herald.wiz.sum.note.plain: Finish places the first post. From then on BakaLoader edits that same post whenever the world changes, and you never need to touch it again.

waystone.wiz.intro.body.lore: A Waystone gives your server a name. Friends type valheim.your-domain.com instead of a raw IP. The name survives IP changes: update one DNS record and every join prompt, copy chip and Discord post follows.
waystone.wiz.intro.body.plain: A domain gives your server a name. Friends type valheim.your-domain.com instead of a raw IP. The name survives IP changes: update one DNS record and every join prompt, copy chip and Discord post follows.

waystone.wiz.intro.need.body.lore: a domain you own (any registrar), or a free dynamic-DNS name (DuckDNS, No-IP). Nothing is bought or installed here. This wizard only teaches your DNS to point at this server.

waystone.wiz.intro.shows.body.lore: Sail Forth join prompts, the Network card, Copy join address, and the Herald's Discord post all prefer the name once it's raised.
waystone.wiz.intro.shows.body.plain: Join prompts, the Network card, Copy join address, and the Discord status post all prefer the name once it is set.

waystone.wiz.remove.title.lore: Lower the Waystone. Join surfaces go back to showing the raw public IP. Your DNS record is untouched.
waystone.wiz.remove.title.plain: Remove the domain. Join surfaces go back to showing the raw public IP. Your DNS record is untouched.

waystone.wiz.name.body.lore: Pick the full name friends will type. A subdomain keeps your main site untouched: valheim.example.com rather than example.com. Dynamic-DNS users: paste the name your provider gave you, like mysaga.duckdns.org.

waystone.wiz.name.input.title.lore: Just the name, with no https:// and no port. Pasting a full URL is fine; it will be trimmed.

waystone.wiz.name.stat.idle.lore: type the name · letters, digits and hyphens, with at least one dot

waystone.wiz.name.stat.bad.lore: not a valid hostname: it needs a dot, no spaces and no ports, like valheim.example.com

waystone.wiz.dns.title.lore: Point the name at this server

waystone.wiz.dns.own.lore: Own domain · add an A record

waystone.wiz.dns.own.step1.lore: open your DNS provider's dashboard (Cloudflare, Namecheap, Porkbun, wherever the domain lives)

waystone.wiz.dns.own.step3.lore: TTL 300-3600 s is fine · on Cloudflare set the cloud to DNS only (grey), because the orange proxy does not carry game traffic

waystone.wiz.dns.ddns.lore: Home connection · IP changes? use dynamic DNS

waystone.wiz.dns.ddns.duckdns.lore: DuckDNS (free): claim yourname.duckdns.org, run their tiny updater so the record follows your IP

waystone.wiz.dns.ddns.noip.lore: No-IP or your router's built-in DDNS page work the same way

waystone.wiz.dns.ddns.cname.lore: own a domain AND have a changing IP? point a CNAME at your dynamic-DNS name

waystone.wiz.dns.note.lore: New records usually answer in a minute or two; some resolvers take up to an hour. The next step checks it live, and you can finish either way and re-check later.

waystone.wiz.check.note.lore: A fresh record can lag behind. If it doesn't resolve yet you can still raise the Waystone now, and it starts working the moment DNS catches up.
waystone.wiz.check.note.plain: A fresh record can lag behind. If it doesn't resolve yet you can still save the domain now, and it starts working the moment DNS catches up.

waystone.wiz.check.stat.failed.lore: the check itself failed, and you can still raise the Waystone
waystone.wiz.check.stat.failed.plain: the check itself failed, and you can still save the domain

waystone.wiz.check.stat.match.lore: the name answers with this server's IP, perfect

waystone.wiz.check.stat.mismatch.lore: the name resolves, but not to this server's public IP: a stale record, a proxy (orange cloud?), or propagation still in flight

waystone.removed.toast.lore: The Waystone falls · back to the raw IP
waystone.removed.toast.plain: Domain removed · back to the raw IP

waystone.wiz.intro.limit.body.lore: Valheim resolves the name but has no SRV support, so the port always travels with it: friends join with {join}.

waystone.wiz.dns.body.lore: Teach DNS that {domain} lives at this server's public IP: {ip}

waystone.wiz.dns.own.step2.lore: add a record: Type A · Name/Host the subdomain part (for valheim.example.com enter valheim) · Value {ip}

waystone.wiz.dns.remember.body.lore: the name only replaces the IP, so friends still need the port ({port}), and port-forwarding stays exactly as it is today.

waystone.wiz.check.stat.unresolved.lore: the name does not resolve yet · give DNS a few minutes, then Check again

world.wg.combat.intro.lore: Sets how much damage you deal and take, and how often you run into higher leveled enemies.

world.wg.combat.veryeasy.explain.lore: You deal 25 percent more damage, enemies deal half their normal damage, and enemies are 10 percent smaller and slower outside dungeons.

world.wg.combat.easy.explain.lore: You deal 10 percent more damage, enemies deal 75 percent of their normal damage, and enemies are 5 percent smaller and slower outside dungeons.

world.wg.combat.normal.explain.lore: Combat plays exactly as the game ships it, with no damage, size or enemy level changes applied.

world.wg.combat.hard.explain.lore: You deal 15 percent less damage, enemies deal 50 percent more, enemies are 10 percent bigger and faster outside dungeons, and enemies are 20 percent more likely to spawn with stars.

world.wg.combat.veryhard.explain.lore: You deal 30 percent less damage, enemies deal double damage, enemies are 20 percent bigger and faster outside dungeons, and enemies are 40 percent more likely to spawn with stars.

world.wg.deathpenalty.intro.lore: Sets what happens to your items and your skills when you die.

world.wg.deathpenalty.casual.explain.lore: You do not drop equipped gear, so only the items you were not wearing go into a tombstone you can recover, and skill loss is cut to 15 percent of the normal amount.

world.wg.deathpenalty.veryeasy.explain.lore: You drop all items, equipped gear included, into a tombstone you can recover, and skill loss is cut to 15 percent of the normal amount.

world.wg.deathpenalty.easy.explain.lore: You drop all items into a tombstone you can recover, and skill loss is half the normal amount.

world.wg.deathpenalty.normal.explain.lore: You drop all items into a tombstone you can recover, and skills are reduced by the standard amount.

world.wg.deathpenalty.hard.explain.lore: Equipped items are dropped into a tombstone you can recover, everything else in your inventory is deleted for good and never reaches the tombstone, and skill loss is 1.5 times the normal amount.

world.wg.deathpenalty.hardcore.explain.lore: Every item you were carrying, equipped or not, is deleted permanently and all of your skills reset to zero, but your character itself is not deleted.

world.wg.resources.intro.lore: Sets how much material you get from gathering and from enemy drops, shown in the game as a multiplier.

world.wg.resources.muchless.explain.lore: Gathering and enemy drops give half the usual amount of materials.

world.wg.resources.less.explain.lore: Gathering and enemy drops give three quarters of the usual amount of materials.

world.wg.resources.normal.explain.lore: Materials drop at the amounts the game was balanced around.

world.wg.resources.more.explain.lore: Gathering and enemy drops give 1.5 times the usual amount of materials.

world.wg.resources.muchmore.explain.lore: Gathering and enemy drops give double the usual amount of materials.

world.wg.resources.most.explain.lore: Gathering and enemy drops give three times the usual amount of materials, the highest setting the game offers.

world.wg.raids.intro.lore: Sets how often enemies come to raid your base, called Raid Rate in the game.

world.wg.raids.none.explain.lore: The timed raid check never runs, so the usual random raids on your base stop happening.

world.wg.raids.muchless.explain.lore: Raids have to wait twice as long before they can trigger and are half as likely on each check.

world.wg.raids.less.explain.lore: Raids have to wait 50 percent longer before they can trigger and are about a third less likely on each check.

world.wg.raids.normal.explain.lore: Raids arrive at the pace the game was balanced around.

world.wg.raids.more.explain.lore: Raids can trigger after 60 percent of the usual wait and are about 1.7 times as likely on each check.

world.wg.raids.muchmore.explain.lore: Raids can trigger after 30 percent of the usual wait and are more than three times as likely on each check.

world.wg.portals.intro.lore: Changes how portals work, from carrying anything through them to having none at all.

world.wg.portals.casual.explain.lore: Allows you to bring all items with you through portals, ore and metal bars included, which skips much of the hauling the world is built around.

world.wg.portals.normal.explain.lore: Portals work as usual, so ore and metal bars still cannot be carried through them.

world.wg.portals.hard.label.lore: No boss portals, blocked during bosses

world.wg.portals.hard.explain.lore: You will not be able to use portals or exit boss dungeons while a boss is active.

world.wg.portals.veryhard.explain.lore: You will not be able to use portals to teleport yourself across the world, so every trip is made on foot or by boat.

world.wg.own_note.lore: BakaLoader clears the world's whole starting key list at every start and then puts back exactly what is stored here: these dials, the five switches, and any other key the world was carrying. A world made in the game client is read once, the first time BakaLoader meets it, so what it already had is brought in rather than wiped. A change made from the in-game console after that is not stored here, so it does not survive a restart.

world.wgs.nobuildcost.line.lore: Building pieces cost nothing to place

world.wgs.nobuildcost.help.lore: Every building piece can be put up without the materials it asks for. Crafting is not part of it: making things at a workbench or a forge is held by a separate key this switch does not set, so crafting still costs what it costs. Anything you place that the game counts as an item or a feast goes with crafting rather than with building.

world.wgs.nobuildcost.help.aria.lore: What the No build cost switch does

world.wgs.playerevents.line.lore: Raids follow each player's own progress

world.wgs.playerevents.help.lore: A raid is normally picked from how far the world has got. With this on the game only sends one at a player it is a possible event for, so everybody meets the raids their own progress has unlocked instead of the world's.

world.wgs.playerevents.help.aria.lore: What the Player based raids switch does

world.wgs.passivemobs.help.lore: Creatures do not go after a player on their own: they do not sense one, nothing landing near them puts them on alert, and they leave what players have built alone. Hit one and it turns on you the way it always did.

world.wgs.passivemobs.help.aria.lore: What the Passive enemies switch does

world.wgs.nomap.line.lore: No minimap and no map at all

world.wgs.nomap.help.lore: The map is switched off for everyone on the server: no minimap in the corner and no full map to open, so people find their way by landmarks.

world.wgs.nomap.help.aria.lore: What the No map switch does

world.wgs.fire.line.lore: Fires throw cinders outside the Ashlands too

world.wgs.fire.help.lore: Fires throw cinders anywhere in the world rather than only in the Ashlands, so a fire can spread where it normally could not. A blow that is mostly fire damage also leaves the burnt drop it would leave in the Ashlands.

world.wgs.fire.help.aria.lore: What the Fire hazards switch does

world.wgs.note.lore: switches are saved with the world, the same way the dials are, and go in the next time the server starts
